parts.name: AMD Kria KV260 Vision AI Starter Kit
parts.accelerator: Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC / programmable logic DPU
parts.software_stack: Vitis AI / Vivado / Vitis / programmable logic
parts.plain_language: KV260 is here as a programmable-architecture laboratory, not because its stock DPU is a great LLM engine. It gives us a relatively affordable way to test custom INT4, ternary/BitNet, sparse-attention or streaming transformer datapaths and measure whether FPGA specialization can beat general-purpose hardware per watt.
parts.source_notes: AMD lists KV260 at US$249 MSRP. The K26 SOM is specified at 7.5W typical / 15W maximum; Vitis AI documentation lists 1.23 TOPS INT8 for the stock B4096 DPU implementation.

parts.name: AMD Versal AI Edge Series Gen 2 platform reference
parts.accelerator: Versal AI Edge Gen 2 AIE-ML v2 + programmable logic
parts.plain_language: Versal Gen 2 is a watch-list platform because it combines Arm CPUs, AI Engines and programmable logic with much higher memory bandwidth than small FPGA kits. It could become interesting for custom transformer engines once affordable boards appear, but it should not receive an LLM score before a real board, price and runtime are resolved.
parts.source_notes: AMD specifies up to 184 dense INT8 TOPS and up to 170GB/s LPDDR5X bandwidth on the largest listed devices. No affordable board price is recorded in this snapshot.

parts.name: AMD Alveo V70 discontinued AI accelerator watch
parts.software_stack: AMD Vitis AI / legacy Alveo support
parts.plain_language: This is exactly the kind of decommissioned datacenter hardware the project should watch. On paper it offers huge inference throughput at 75W, but AMD has discontinued it and limited future support. It only becomes attractive if a cheap used price and a practical transformer software path are both demonstrated.
parts.source_notes: AMD marks V70 discontinued and lists 404 TOPS INT8, 202 TOPS BF16, 76.8GB/s external DDR bandwidth and 75W TDP. No trustworthy current used price was resolved in this snapshot.

parts.name: AMD Alveo U50 8GB HBM2 FPGA accelerator watch
parts.host_requirements: PCIe host with server-style forced airflow; custom Vitis/Vivado design or compatible accelerator stack
parts.software_stack: AMD Vitis / Vivado / OpenCL / custom RTL-HLS
parts.plain_language: U50 is a particularly interesting pure-FPGA research target because its 8GB HBM2 can feed custom logic at far higher bandwidth than ordinary DDR. It is not a plug-and-play LLM card: its value would come from implementing or porting a transformer datapath, so used price and software effort must be counted before it can compete with simpler GPUs/APUs.
parts.source_notes: AMD documentation lists 8GB HBM2, 316GB/s bandwidth and a 75W maximum power limit. Current secondary-market price is intentionally unresolved in this snapshot.
